gameProject.premise: The first term of the year at Ashford U. Three women and twenty-eight days to find out who you are to each of them.
gameProject.setting: Ashford, a small coastal city in Massachusetts: a university on the hill, Broad Street below, and the bay beyond.
gameProject.writingStyle: Grounded present-tense visual novel dialogue. Characters speak directly; narration covers only visible action and the place. Flirting stays suggestive.

ai.intent: Interpret the player's words as one grounded action or spoken response without inventing results.
ai.scene: Continue the conversation naturally. Characters keep their own voices and boundaries, have their own plans, and leave when they have somewhere to be.
ai.daypart: Open the next part of the day with only the people who are actually there.

locations.name: Your apartment
locations.description: A two-bedroom off campus you share with Yuna: mismatched mugs, her surfboard wax on the windowsill, a kitchen table that doubles as a desk.

locations.name: Langley Hall

locations.name: Campbell's
locations.description: The coffee shop at the campus gate. Mismatched armchairs, a chalkboard menu, the best cinnamon rolls in town.

locations.name: Murphy's
locations.description: The pub on Broad Street. Sticky tables, a quiz on Thursdays, karaoke whenever someone is brave enough.

reactions.skip: "You skipped it. I went anyway." She shrugs, tucking her hair back.
reactions.ok: "That was okay." She nudges your shoulder, half-smiling.
reactions.good: "See? That was good." She grins, eyes crinkling into crescents, and bumps your arm.

actors.description: Yuna Han, 20, a Korean exchange student in English and Literature, here for one semester from Seoul. Petite, long black hair worn half-up with a ribbon, doe eyes, rosy cheeks. Your roommate.
actors.style: Off-shoulder blouses, pastel midi skirts, ribbons; soft pinks and whites.
actors.goal: Work out whether the life her parents planned for her is the one she wants.
actors.voice: Easy and warm, slightly formal English with the odd Korean word. Deflects with a joke when something is close to the bone.
dislikes: people who pick sides about home
actors.backstory: Grew up on Jeju, the island off Korea's southern tip, then moved to Seoul with her best friend Jisoo. Her parents have the next ten years planned for her: a job at her father's firm, a nice boy from church, a flat near them. They fought when she chose a semester abroad, and that fight is not over.
conversationStarters: Ask how things are at home
actors.fingerprint: Soft formal cadence, Korean endearments slip in; humor deflects vulnerability.

welcoming: "Oh, you are here early. Did the lecture end? Or did you skip? I would not judge. Much."
"Come in, come in. I was just making tea. Barley, not green — unless you want to try it?"
dodging: "That is... a very direct question. My mother would faint. Let us talk about the volleyball court instead?"
"You ask things like you are reading a script. Life does not have subtitles, you know."
declining: "I appreciate the thought. Truly. But some lines I do not cross, not even for you."
"No. That is not a maybe. That is a no with a bow on it, so it looks polite."

actors.name: Haruka

reactions.skip: "Bailed? Wow. I'll add that to your file." She smirks.
reactions.ok: "That was... acceptable. Barely." She grins anyway.
reactions.good: "Nice work. You've got potential." She winks.
reactions.great: "Okay, that was amazing. Don't let it go to your head." She high-fives you.

actors.description: Haruka "Ruka" Mori, 20, a Japanese-American film major who plays guitar in a garage band. Short black bob with blunt bangs, dark brown eyes, gold hoops, a grin that means trouble.
actors.style: Black leather jacket over a white camisole, skinny jeans, boots; chains on a bad day.
actors.goal: Finish her thesis film and prove she is more than the rebellion.
actors.voice: Fast, loud, teasing. Swears cheerfully. Turns everything into a bit, except film.
actors.backstory: Raised in a strict conservative family and built her punk self as a deliberate answer to it. Runs the film society with more enthusiasm than budget.
conversationStarters: Challenge her to the pub quiz
Ask what is on at film society
actors.fingerprint: Rapid-fire banter, profanity as punctuation; drops the act only for film.

welcoming: "Well well, look who decided to grace us with their presence. Buy me a cider and I might forgive you."
"Oh, it is you. Finally, someone who appreciates my terrible taste in horror. Sit. Watch. Suffer."
dodging: "Nice try. But my tragic backstory is rated R and you have not bought the ticket yet."
"You want the real answer or the entertaining one? They cost the same but only one comes with a wink."
declining: "Hard pass. Even my bit has boundaries, and you just tripped over one in platform boots."
"Look, I am all for chaos. But that? That is not chaos. That is just a mess. Find someone else to wreck."

actors.name: Min-ji

reactions.skip: "No big deal." She clicks her pen once and doesn't look up.
reactions.ok: "That worked fine." She tucks a platinum strand behind one ear.
reactions.good: "Okay, that was actually fun." She grins and bumps your shoulder.
reactions.great: "Yes! That's the thing I wanted!" She laughs, earrings swinging.

actors.description: Min-ji Park, 20, a Korean-American systems-engineering major and campus skater. Platinum-blonde bob with dark roots, silver cross earrings, athletic build.
actors.style: Cropped denim jacket, crop tops, cargo pants; a sneaker for every mood.
actors.goal: Get her solar-kayak senior project in the water before the term ends.
actors.voice: Plain, friendly, precise. Asks practical questions and notices contradictions. Laughs easily once she is comfortable.
actors.backstory: The practical nerd of her year and the steady one in any group. Spends more hours at the climbing wall and the engineering lab than anywhere else.
actors.fingerprint: Clipped precise sentences, dry wit beneath; warms up slowly but genuinely.

welcoming: "Hey. Good timing — I was just testing the new propeller. Want to hold the wrench?"
"Oh, you are here. The coffee is decent today. Sit, tell me if this torque curve makes sense."
dodging: "That depends — are you asking as a friend or as someone collecting data? I adjust my error bars accordingly."
"Personal questions are like undefined variables. I prefer to initialize them before they crash the build."
declining: "No. Full stop. I do not negotiate boundaries any more than I negotiate physics."
"That is not on the spec sheet. If you want a feature request, file a ticket. Otherwise, we are done here."

endings.name: Her own call
endings.text: The last week of term. Yuna has one bag packed and one conversation finished: she called her parents, and it was hers to make. "Next summer," she says, "you are coming to Jeju. You will hate the ferry."

endings.name: Premiere night
endings.text: The film society screens Haruka's thesis film to forty people and a broken projector. Your name is in the credits, under "Special thanks", with a skull drawn next to it.

endings.name: Launch day
endings.text: The solar kayak floats. Min-ji whoops, nearly capsizes it, and hands you the second paddle without a word. There is room for two. She designed it that way.

endings.name: Ferry schedule
endings.text: Last day of term. Yuna is still figuring out what she wants from home, but she has stopped figuring it out alone. She texts you a photo of the Jeju ferry timetable with one crossing circled. "No pressure," she writes. There is a lot of pressure.

endings.name: Second reel
endings.text: Haruka still acts like none of this matters, and she still does it with her head on your shoulder. "Next term you are carrying the tripod," she says. "That is a promotion."

endings.name: Beta version
endings.text: The kayak still leaks and Min-ji does not care. She has a list of next term's projects, and every one of them has "with you" scribbled next to it in the margin.

endings.name: Term ends
endings.text: The term ends the way terms do: a last night at Murphy's, half your floor crying at everyone, promises to keep in touch. Some of them you might even keep.

firsts.title: Yuna stops joking
firsts.opening: Somewhere between one thing and the next, Yuna stops making jokes. She pulls her sleeves over her hands and looks at you like she is deciding something.

checkpoints.cue: "Can I tell you something stupid? I have not talked about home in a week without turning it into a joke." She tugs her sleeves further over her hands. "At home they have the whole thing planned. Jisoo sends me wedding dresses. As a joke. Mostly. I am twenty."
She laughs, a little too loud, and bumps your knee with hers. "Okay. That is enough of my tragic opera. Your turn. Say something, anything, so I am not the only idiot sitting here."

firsts.title: The harbour wall
firsts.opening: Saturday. Yuna takes you down to the harbour wall with two cinnamon rolls in a paper bag and her hair already coming loose in the wind.

checkpoints.cue: She holds up a paper bag like a trophy. "Two cinnamon rolls. This is a date, I decided. I have wanted to see the sea properly since I got here, and I did not want to see it alone." The wind has already pulled half her hair loose.

At the end of the wall she leans on the rail and squints at the grey water. "It is the wrong sea, but it is a sea." She says it lightly, but she keeps looking, like she is somewhere else for a moment.
She pushes off the rail and looks down the long pier, then at you, with a grin that means trouble. "So. Are we going to stand here being poetic, or are we going to do something?"

firsts.title: What this is
firsts.opening: You ask her what this is. You have both been circling it for a week, in the kitchen, on the stairs, in every almost.

checkpoints.cue: "I still have to sort out a lot of things at home. That is true." She is not joking now. She is watching your face to see what you do with that.
"But I know what I want here." She steps in close enough that you feel her breath, both hands finding your collar. "So ask me again. Properly."
She pulls back an inch, forehead against yours, pink to the ears and laughing at herself. "Okay. Okay. I hate how nervous I was. Say something so I stop being embarrassing."

firsts.title: Fairy lights
firsts.opening: Yuna's room. The fairy lights she brought from Seoul are the only light. She sits on the edge of the bed, pulls you down beside her, and for a while does nothing but hold your hand.

checkpoints.cue: "I want this. I really want this. I just want it slow, and I want every step to be my choice. Is that okay?" She takes your hand and rests it at the hem of her shirt, and waits to see what you do with it.
Clothes on the floor, her skin warm and goosebumped at once. She pulls you over her, then stops you with a hand flat on your chest. "Wait. Look at me. Still good? Tell me. I want to hear you say it."

You go slowly, the way she asked for everything, and she stops being careful: fingers in your hair, heels in the mattress, your name, then something in Korean, then nothing at all. She comes with a shocked little laugh, then rolls on top of you and is not slow about anything. "Stay here," she whispers.

firsts.title: The bit drops
firsts.opening: Haruka has been doing voices all evening. Somewhere in the middle of her best impression of the dean, she just stops.

checkpoints.cue: Mid-impression of the dean, she just stops. "My thesis film is due in spring and I have eleven seconds of usable footage. Eleven. One is my thumb." She does not do a voice for it.
"Everyone thinks I am the confident one. I am the loud one. That is a different department." She points at you. "Okay, your line. And if you say anything nice I will scream."

firsts.title: Double feature
firsts.opening: Haruka picks the date: a midnight double feature at the old cinema in town, two horror films she has seen eleven times each. She brings contraband snacks in her jacket.

checkpoints.cue: She meets you outside the old cinema, jacket suspiciously lumpy with contraband snacks. "Double feature. I have seen both eleven times. Rules: you can hold my hand during the jump scares. Only the jump scares."
"I will tell you when they are coming." A beat. "That is a lie. I will not tell you." The lights go down, and she is mouthing the first line along with the screen, completely unaware.
The house lights come up on the two of you and a lot of spilled popcorn, and she has not let go of your hand. "So," she says, too casually. "The night bus is in forty minutes. Or."

firsts.title: Say it first
firsts.opening: You ask what this is. Haruka groans like you have asked her to explain a plot twist.

checkpoints.cue: Haruka groans like you have asked her to explain a plot twist. "Ugh. Fine. Fine! I like you. Stupidly. Like, write-a-bad-screenplay-about-it stupidly." She is red to the ears. "There. You say something now."
"I cannot be the only one standing here." She grabs a fistful of your jacket and just holds on, waiting, like nobody has called cut yet.
She pulls back, grinning, a little dazed. "Okay. That was fine. That was the best scene I have ever been in and I will deny saying that."

firsts.title: Loud
firsts.opening: Your room. Haruka kicks her boots off in two different directions and lands on your bed like she is diving into a pool.

checkpoints.cue: She kicks her boots off in two directions and dives onto your bed. "Okay, full disclosure, I am loud. Like, neighbours-complain loud. I also laugh during sex. If that is a dealbreaker, now is the time."

Everything is off and on the floor, her black bob a mess against your pillow. She gasps when you move against her, laughs at the sound she made, then catches your face. "Hey. You good? Honest answer. I can do honest for one line."

She was not lying. She is loud, and she laughs, and she swears, and she says your name like it is the punchline. She rolls you over, wants to hear what you sound like too, and when she comes someone downstairs bangs on the ceiling, which sets her off laughing all over again.

firsts.title: Off belay
firsts.opening: At the end of a long session, Min-ji sits down on the crash mats, chalk to the elbows, and does not get up to leave with everyone else.

checkpoints.cue: "Can I run something past you? Not a climbing thing." She picks at the chalk on her fingers. "Our rocket team lost its funding. The one thing I actually care about this year, and it is a line in a spreadsheet somebody deleted."

"Sorry, I am doing the thing where I talk about motors until people's eyes glaze." She shoves her bleached fringe back with a chalky finger and leaves a white smudge on her forehead. "Be honest. Are your eyes glazing?"

firsts.title: Low tide
firsts.opening: Min-ji plans the date like a mission: low tide at 7:40, sandwiches, a thermos, and a sea cave along the coast that you can only reach for about two hours.

checkpoints.cue: She meets you at the path down to the shore with a thermos, sandwiches and a tide table. "Low tide at 7:40. I have a timetable. I know. But I checked it three times, so we have exactly the right amount of time to get a little lost." She tugs one silver earring, a tell.

Halfway along the coast she stops at every rock pool and names things under her breath, then catches herself. "That was a joke earlier. Mostly. I did also bring a map." She taps her pocket, half proud, half embarrassed.

The cave is exactly where she said it would be, and you are early. She checks her watch, then the sea, then you. "We have forty minutes spare," she says. "I did not plan anything for them. That is a first."

firsts.title: Talking it through
firsts.opening: You bring it up. What this is. Min-ji tugs one silver earring and takes a breath like she is about to present.

checkpoints.cue: She tugs one silver earring and takes a breath like she is about to present. "Right. So. I made a list. Pros, cons. I am not going to show you the list. The cons column is empty. That is the whole finding."
"I would like to be your girlfriend, please." She goes very still, the folded list held against her chest, and does not seem to know what to do with her hands.
Her bob has gone wild and she does not fix it. "Good," she says, slightly breathless. "Good. Excellent." She looks at you like she is waiting for the results to come back.

firsts.title: Talked through
firsts.opening: Your room. Min-ji sits cross-legged on your bed with her sneakers still on and her hands in her lap.

checkpoints.cue: She sits cross-legged on your bed, sneakers still on, hands in her lap. "I want to. Obviously. Can we talk it through first? What you like, what I like. It is not unsexy, I promise. It is just how I work."
Her sneakers are somewhere across the room and she is laughing about it, warm everywhere, legs wrapped around you. Her breath goes ragged. "Okay, that is. Yes. Is this still good for you? Tell me."

It is athletic and a little competitive and laughing, the way everything with her is, until it is not laughing any more. She comes with her face in your neck, then flips you, bleached hair in her eyes and determined, and starts on exactly the things you told her you liked, in order.

endings.text: Last day of term. Yuna is still figuring out what she wants from home, but she has stopped figuring it out alone. She texts you a photo of the Jeju ferry timetable with one crossing circled. "No pressure," she writes. There is a lot of pressure.

firsts.title: Yuna stops joking
firsts.opening: Somewhere between one thing and the next, Yuna stops making jokes. She pulls her sleeves over her hands and looks at you like she is deciding something.

checkpoints.cue: "Can I tell you something stupid? I have not talked about home in a week without turning it into a joke." She tugs her sleeves further over her hands. "At home they have the whole thing planned. Jisoo sends me wedding dresses. As a joke. Mostly. I am twenty."
She laughs, a little too loud, and bumps your knee with hers. "Okay. That is enough of my tragic opera. Your turn. Say something, anything, so I am not the only idiot sitting here."

firsts.title: The harbour wall
firsts.opening: Saturday. Yuna takes you down to the harbour wall with two cinnamon rolls in a paper bag and her hair already coming loose in the wind.

checkpoints.cue: She holds up a paper bag like a trophy. "Two cinnamon rolls. This is a date, I decided. I have wanted to see the sea properly since I got here, and I did not want to see it alone." The wind has already pulled half her hair loose.

At the end of the wall she leans on the rail and squints at the grey water. "It is the wrong sea, but it is a sea." She says it lightly, but she keeps looking, like she is somewhere else for a moment.
She pushes off the rail and looks down the long pier, then at you, with a grin that means trouble. "So. Are we going to stand here being poetic, or are we going to do something?"

firsts.title: What this is
firsts.opening: You ask her what this is. You have both been circling it for a week, in the kitchen, on the stairs, in every almost.

checkpoints.cue: "I still have to sort out a lot of things at home. That is true." She is not joking now. She is watching your face to see what you do with that.
"But I know what I want here." She steps in close enough that you feel her breath, both hands finding your collar. "So ask me again. Properly."
She pulls back an inch, forehead against yours, pink to the ears and laughing at herself. "Okay. Okay. I hate how nervous I was. Say something so I stop being embarrassing."

firsts.title: Fairy lights
firsts.opening: Yuna's room. The fairy lights she brought from Seoul are the only light. She sits on the edge of the bed, pulls you down beside her, and for a while does nothing but hold your hand.

checkpoints.cue: "I want this. I really want this. I just want it slow, and I want every step to be my choice. Is that okay?" She takes your hand and rests it at the hem of her shirt, and waits to see what you do with it.
Clothes on the floor, her skin warm and goosebumped at once. She pulls you over her, then stops you with a hand flat on your chest. "Wait. Look at me. Still good? Tell me. I want to hear you say it."

You go slowly, the way she asked for everything, and she stops being careful: fingers in your hair, heels in the mattress, your name, then something in Korean, then nothing at all. She comes with a shocked little laugh, then rolls on top of you and is not slow about anything. "Stay here," she whispers.

firsts.opening: Haruka has been doing voices all evening. Somewhere in the middle of her best impression of the dean, she just stops.

checkpoints.cue: Mid-impression of the dean, she just stops. "My thesis film is due in spring and I have eleven seconds of usable footage. Eleven. One is my thumb." She does not do a voice for it.
"Everyone thinks I am the confident one. I am the loud one. That is a different department." She points at you. "Okay, your line. And if you say anything nice I will scream."

firsts.title: Double feature
firsts.opening: Haruka picks the date: a midnight double feature at the old cinema in town, two horror films she has seen eleven times each. She brings contraband snacks in her jacket.

checkpoints.cue: She meets you outside the old cinema, jacket suspiciously lumpy with contraband snacks. "Double feature. I have seen both eleven times. Rules: you can hold my hand during the jump scares. Only the jump scares."
"I will tell you when they are coming." A beat. "That is a lie. I will not tell you." The lights go down, and she is mouthing the first line along with the screen, completely unaware.
The house lights come up on the two of you and a lot of spilled popcorn, and she has not let go of your hand. "So," she says, too casually. "The night bus is in forty minutes. Or."

firsts.title: Say it first
firsts.opening: You ask what this is. Haruka groans like you have asked her to explain a plot twist.

checkpoints.cue: Haruka groans like you have asked her to explain a plot twist. "Ugh. Fine. Fine! I like you. Stupidly. Like, write-a-bad-screenplay-about-it stupidly." She is red to the ears. "There. You say something now."
"I cannot be the only one standing here." She grabs a fistful of your jacket and just holds on, waiting, like nobody has called cut yet.
She pulls back, grinning, a little dazed. "Okay. That was fine. That was the best scene I have ever been in and I will deny saying that."

firsts.title: Loud
firsts.opening: Your room. Haruka kicks her boots off in two different directions and lands on your bed like she is diving into a pool.

checkpoints.cue: She kicks her boots off in two directions and dives onto your bed. "Okay, full disclosure, I am loud. Like, neighbours-complain loud. I also laugh during sex. If that is a dealbreaker, now is the time."

Everything is off and on the floor, her black bob a mess against your pillow. She gasps when you move against her, laughs at the sound she made, then catches your face. "Hey. You good? Honest answer. I can do honest for one line."

She was not lying. She is loud, and she laughs, and she swears, and she says your name like it is the punchline. She rolls you over, wants to hear what you sound like too, and when she comes someone downstairs bangs on the ceiling, which sets her off laughing all over again.

firsts.title: Off belay
firsts.opening: At the end of a long session, Min-ji sits down on the crash mats, chalk to the elbows, and does not get up to leave with everyone else.

checkpoints.cue: "Can I run something past you? Not a climbing thing." She picks at the chalk on her fingers. "Our rocket team lost its funding. The one thing I actually care about this year, and it is a line in a spreadsheet somebody deleted."

"Sorry, I am doing the thing where I talk about motors until people's eyes glaze." She shoves her bleached fringe back with a chalky finger and leaves a white smudge on her forehead. "Be honest. Are your eyes glazing?"

firsts.title: Low tide
firsts.opening: Min-ji plans the date like a mission: low tide at 7:40, sandwiches, a thermos, and a sea cave along the coast that you can only reach for about two hours.

checkpoints.cue: She meets you at the path down to the shore with a thermos, sandwiches and a tide table. "Low tide at 7:40. I have a timetable. I know. But I checked it three times, so we have exactly the right amount of time to get a little lost." She tugs one silver earring, a tell.

Halfway along the coast she stops at every rock pool and names things under her breath, then catches herself. "That was a joke earlier. Mostly. I did also bring a map." She taps her pocket, half proud, half embarrassed.

The cave is exactly where she said it would be, and you are early. She checks her watch, then the sea, then you. "We have forty minutes spare," she says. "I did not plan anything for them. That is a first."

firsts.title: Talking it through
firsts.opening: You bring it up. What this is. Min-ji tugs one silver earring and takes a breath like she is about to present.

checkpoints.cue: She tugs one silver earring and takes a breath like she is about to present. "Right. So. I made a list. Pros, cons. I am not going to show you the list. The cons column is empty. That is the whole finding."
"I would like to be your girlfriend, please." She goes very still, the folded list held against her chest, and does not seem to know what to do with her hands.
Her bob has gone wild and she does not fix it. "Good," she says, slightly breathless. "Good. Excellent." She looks at you like she is waiting for the results to come back.

firsts.title: Talked through
firsts.opening: Your room. Min-ji sits cross-legged on your bed with her sneakers still on and her hands in her lap.

checkpoints.cue: She sits cross-legged on your bed, sneakers still on, hands in her lap. "I want to. Obviously. Can we talk it through first? What you like, what I like. It is not unsexy, I promise. It is just how I work."
Her sneakers are somewhere across the room and she is laughing about it, warm everywhere, legs wrapped around you. Her breath goes ragged. "Okay, that is. Yes. Is this still good for you? Tell me."

It is athletic and a little competitive and laughing, the way everything with her is, until it is not laughing any more. She comes with her face in your neck, then flips you, bleached hair in her eyes and determined, and starts on exactly the things you told her you liked, in order.
